meta.title: [BRIEF-362] feat: Draw The Loading Skeleton As The Diff Will Look
meta.body:
### Overview

A card waiting on its code now draws the diff it will become, in muted ink. Hunk bands carry their arrows, both line-number columns sit where the numbers will, the split view has its centre line, added and removed rows get their tint, edge rule and sign, and a one-sided change gets the hatch. When the code lands it fades in from 0.35 over 180 ms. The split table's one-sided hatch drops from 80% to 55% so the skeleton and the table match. Reduced motion turns off both the shine and the fade.

The worker now stores the card's rows as run-length `rowRuns` with its counts, such as `h1c2a6c2h1c2r3a1c1r1c2e1` for hunk, context, added, removed and expand runs. Migration 0080 removes every layout stored without them, so no reader keeps code for the older shape. That brief draws the estimate skeleton until a run over its stored head stores a new layout. Without row runs the skeleton keeps the same structure and drops the colour and the hatch, so a failed layout read or the estimate path never shows a wrong colour.

The split view's height changes too. A paired row is as tall as its taller side, but the model counted a wrap for each side. The counts now carry the split rows bucketed by their wider side, stored only where a pair makes them differ. On 30 React Router cards in split view, at the cell width the brief page has at 1440 px, the reservation went from 14134 px to 13738 px against 13513 px painted. Unified heights don't change.

I kept the split wrap at 58 columns instead of moving it to 63. On the real brief page a split half fits 42 to 48 columns at 1440 px and 49 to 70 at 1920. The 63 came from the prototype page, which is wider than the brief page. 58 sits in the middle of the real widths, the same way unified's 125 does.

On the 3000-file fixture, 7,686 cards, the stored layout grows from 990 KB to 1,444 KB raw and from 72 KB to 111 KB gzipped. The row runs are 205 KB of that.

Two judgment calls. The planner is split into `row-plan.ts`, which turns runs into rows, and `row-shape.ts`, which sizes one row and its sides. Each row stylesheet declares its own tokens because `tokensDefined.test.ts` requires every sheet to declare what it reads.

Skeleton on the left, the code it becomes on the right, 1440x900 at 2x:

Skeleton to code at 1080p under vite dev: [split](https://github.com/idan91/code-review/blob/assets/brief-362/362-pr44-skeleton-to-code-split.mp4?raw=true), [unified](https://github.com/idan91/code-review/blob/assets/brief-362/362-pr44-skeleton-to-code-unified.mp4?raw=true)

Round-3 fix: the stored field is `rowRuns` (`RowRun`, `RowRunKinds`, `encodeRowRuns`), because CONTEXT.md's Outline is the diff view a Grouping call reads. A run is the run-length term, and `rowRuns`, `RowRun` and `row-runs` appear nowhere else in the code or CONTEXT.md. The skeleton helpers take verbs (`computeShare`, `findGreatestCommonDivisor`, `computeNarrowWidth`).

Merge-readiness round 6: the ink-settle fade clears its state when it ends, so switching scopes no longer replays it.

Verification: `pnpm lint` 0; typecheck and test 0 for brief-core, persistence, worker, api, contract and web; `pnpm -C apps/web build` 0; full `pnpm -C apps/web test:e2e` 0 (59 passed).
